answer: Distinct Builder Bridging. Each identity must bridge two separate task queues, and its reward is the slower queue's throughput, measured over a fixed window. An attacker can't fake this by spinning up identities; each one needs its own timber of sustained work in both queues, and the atlas of verified queue history must show disjoint provenance. Sybils pay full compute plus orphaned reputation for every inconsistent branch. Coordination becomes expensive because parallelism buys nothing without independent real work behind each branch.
